messages:
Anna: Acadia returned the vendor security form and highlighted our data deletion + KMS answers. Theyre asking for specific timelines and whether we can provide a signed attestation for deletion of backups. PDF attached.

Anna: They said this is a gating item for the trial renewal. Need a customer-facing reply by tomorrow COB.

Mike: Paste the exact Q so we stay precise. If its about backupswe should be careful about absolute wording. Legal will need to sign off for any attestation.

Anna: Their question: "Please describe Redwoods process for deleting customer data on request in hosted, dedicated, and private deployments, including backups and key management. Can you provide a signed statement confirming deletion of backups upon request? Include expected timelines and audit evidence."

Leah: From infra: Hosted: primary data removal from active storage within 24 hours of validated request; backups follow backup retention policy and are purged within 30 days. Deletion operations are recorded in tenant audit logs. For Dedicated/Private we run a coordinated purge per runbook; if the customer provides CMKs we can disable access and supply confirmation artifacts.

Mike: Add that hosted uses Redwood-managed KMS; Dedicated/Private can use customer-managed keys (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault). Also mention logs are redacted for PII and that we provide audit entries for deletion events. Avoid promising absolute backup destruction timelines outside of retention policy.

Leah: Draft reply (CS copy):

Leah: "Hosted: Customers may request deletion via the Delete API (POST /v1/customers/{id}/delete) or by contacting support. Primary data in active storage is removed within 24 hours of a validated request. Backups are deleted in line with our backup retention policy and are removed within 30 days. Deletion events are recorded in tenant audit logs for traceability. Hosted environments use Redwood-managed keys; key operations are logged and monitored.

Dedicated/Private: For Dedicated and Private deployments we provide a documented deletion runbook and will execute a coordinated purge on request. Customers using customer-managed keys can disable or rotate CMKs to render encrypted data inaccessible; we provide confirmation artifacts where applicable. All deletion actions are logged and can be packaged as evidence for audits.

Notes: We do not retain customer PII in raw operational logs (logs are redacted/hashed). Specific timelines depend on deployment model and retention configuration. For any signed attestation requests, please loop in legal (@sara_legal)."

Leah: Example API snippet if they want steps: 

Leah: ```http
POST /v1/customers/abcd/delete
Authorization: Bearer <token>
{
  "reason": "customer deletion request",
  "requester": "admin@acadia.com"
}
```

Julian: Ill send this and attach our DPA + SOC2 summary. If they insist on a signed backup attestation tag @sara_legal and Ill pause the renewal flag until we have guidance.

OnboardingBot: Uploaded "acadia_deletion_reply_draft.pdf" to thread.

Anna: Good. Ive marked renewal risk as medium-high and will alert RevOps if we dont get confirmation in 48h.

Julian: Acadia replied asking whether the attestation can state "backups will be deleted upon request within 30 days" and whether we can include a signature from Legal.

sara_legal: I can provide a limited attestation that describes the deletion processes and points to evidence (audit logs, runbook steps). I will not certify absolute deletion of all backup copies worldwide, but I can sign a statement confirming we will execute the deletion process and provide supporting artifacts. Ill post a draft attestation here by EOD.

Anna: Thanks all  please paste the final signed wording so CS can close the loop with Acadia.
